utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Today is Monday, February 23rd, 2009. I'd like to say good morning to Mr. Stojic, Mr. Praljak, Mr. Petkovic. I'd like to say good afternoon to the lawyers, in particular Mr. Khan who's come from very far. I'd like to also greet all of the representatives of the OTP, the witness who is waiting to be sworn in. Before we swear in the witness, I would like to give the floor to the Registrar who has four IC numbers to give us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Some parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through witness Vegar Veso. The list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit IC 926; the list submitted by 3D shall be Exhibit IC 927; and the list submitted by 4D shall be given Exhibit IC 928. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Registrar. I would like to read a very brief oral decision regarding the witness Kvesic. This witness is to testify on February 27th [as interpreted]. The Praljak Defence has asked for 15 to 20 minutes for this witness in order to be able to carry out the examination-in-chief under Article 92 ter. The Chamber grants this request to carry out an examination-in-chief under Article 92 ter of the rules and regulations and has decided following: Stojic Defence will have one hour for the examination-in-chief of this witness; the other Defence teams will have an overall time of 30 minutes for the cross; and the Prosecution will have one hour. Then the Praljak Defence will have 20 minutes for the examination-in-chief under Article 92 ter; the other Defence teams will have an overall time of 15 minutes; and the Prosecution will have 30 minutes. I see Mr. Scott has risen. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Mr. President, each of Your Honours, counsel, all those in and around the courtroom. Your Honour, in terms of the Prosecution's witness -- excuse me, exhibit list for the witness Vegar, I'm afraid we're still finalising that and we didn't quite make it before -- by 2.15. I've talked with counsel for Mr. Stojic, and they've been gracious enough to indicate they have no disagreement or objection. If we could file that by the end of the court day, that would be appreciated. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours and everybody else in the courtroom. The Defence of General Praljak is cognisant of the time given for the witness or that we requested earlier on, but for organisational purposes and to be able to manage my time, I'd like to tell the Court that we'll be finished with the witness in three or four minutes because we are not going to have any additional questions to his statement, so we're just going to do a formal verification of the statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Witness, could you please stand in order to say the oath, please. Could you please declare your name and first name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Bruno Pinjuh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your date of birth, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 17th of September, 1958.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified before a Tribunal, or is it the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have never testified before a Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. What is your profession or occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a pensioner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're retired. What are you retired from? Were you in the army? Did you work for the administration? Did you work for a private company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From 1978, I worked in a school as a teacher, and during the war, I performed the duties that I was given, and I am a military retiree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So you are retired from the military. Would you please take the oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me give you some information rapidly, but I'm certain that Madam Nozica has perhaps already told you this. You are going to be answering the questions she's going to put to you. After the examination-in-chief, the other Defence counsel for the accused may ask you questions. It may also occur that the four judges you see before you will ask additional questions, and the Prosecutor who is seated to your right, there are two representatives of the Prosecution here today, but only one of them will cross-examine you. You have taken the oath, and, therefore, you are a witness before the justice system. You will have no contact with anyone else, and if your testimony continues tomorrow, you must spend the evening quietly in your hotel room without telephoning to anyone, without sharing with anyone what you have testified today. Of course, you can call your wife or other members of your family to let them know that everything is okay. That's all. We will be having a break every hour and a half, a half an hour break so that you can rest if at any point you feel comfortable, and of course this could occur. It happens to the Judges, so it can also happen to a witness. Just let us know, raise your hand, and we will have an additional break. That's what I wanted to tell you at this point in order for this hearing to take place in a constructive fashion and so that we not have any particular issues. Madam Nozica, I see you are ready. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good afternoon Mr. Pinjuh.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, and greetings to everybody in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As Judge Antonetti has just explained to you, I'm going to be asking you some questions over the next two hours; that is to say, we have a total of two hours for your examination, and I've already mentioned a technical matter, but I'll repeat it now, and that is that we have to pause, you and I, between my question and your answer so that everything we say can be entered into the transcript. Now, Mr. Pinjuh, I'm going to go through your CV briefly. As you've already said, in 1978 you completed the pedagogical academy in Rijeka or the teachers training academy; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For the transcript, the town was Rijeka. And you became employed that same year, in 1978, in Cerin, the primary school there in Citluk municipality, as a teacher?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In 1992, you were a member of the 4th Company of the HVO Citluk; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what period that was?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: From the beginning of April until the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And that same year on the 1st of June - 1992 is the year we're talking about - the HVO of Citluk municipality appointed you chief of the Defence Department in Citluk; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So until the end of 1993, you performed those duties, and at the beginning of 1993, you were appointed chief of the defence department of Citluk in Citluk; right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber how you came to be appointed chief and at whose proposal and who actually appointed you?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: That was at the proposal of the municipal defence council and municipality assembly of Citluk.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And did the chief of the Defence Department of Mostar put your name forward?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Not in 1992, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, I'm talking about the beginning of 1993 when the head of the Defence Department appointed you chief of the Defence Department in Citluk, what was the procedure?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: The chief of the superior administration which was superior to me in Mostar put forward my name, made the proposal, and then Citluk municipality approved it, and then after that I was appointed by Mr. Stojic, the head of the Defence Department, and it was the head or chief of the Defence Department -- defence office.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So chief of the defence office in Citluk; right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you stayed in that position until July 1994 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a technical question. These issues are very complex, and we want to be perfectly clear and to advance step by step. If I have understood correctly - but please do correct me if I have misunderstood - Mr. Stojic appointed you to this function, to this post, but he appointed you upon proposal by the municipal council of Citluk. Does this mean that if the municipal council of Citluk had not proposed you, Mr. Stojic would not have been able to appoint you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the head appointed me at the proposal of the chief of the administration for the Defence of Mostar with agreement from the municipal council of Citluk; and quite possibly, I wouldn't have been appointed had the municipal council of Citluk not agreed to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your response is the opposite to what you said to the question put to you by the lawyer. You have just said that Mr. Stojic appointed you upon proposal of the municipality of Citluk. Could you tell us slowly, exactly how things occurred, how it took place because it's extremely important. We cannot afford to make a mistake. Could you please tell us again exactly how you were appointed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The procedure was as follows: The chief of the administration of Mostar, which was the superior body to me, defence administration, gave the proposal, put me forward, and the municipal council agrees or does not agree, approves or does not approve, and only after that does the head make the appointment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. But if the municipal council of Citluk said they didn't agree, could Mr. Stojic have appointed you just the same? Are you absolutely certain?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We still don't seem to have the answer on record in the transcript. In response to Judge Antonetti's question, the answer was no. The Judge asked are you absolutely certain, and the witness's answer was, yes, he is certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is that right, Mr. Pinjuh? Is what I've just said correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: As we are at this, I also found this rather interesting. Could you explain, Mr. Pinjuh, why it was the chief of the defence administration in Mostar who proposed you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume that was because I was already doing work of that kind, and so he thought that I'd be up to the job and be able to tackle the duties I would be assigned in future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. That is a good, fitting answer. I had something different in mind. My question went to the organisation of the military administration. We have heard quite a bit about the organisation of the Ministry of Defence, and now comes up administration, the chief of administration Mostar, which must be something that is not the Ministry of Defence. Is it part of the Ministry of Defence? Is it subordinated to the Ministry of Defence? Is Citluk within an area that Mostar has higher responsibility for? I hope I made it clear what my concern is, and thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The defence administration of Mostar is a military and territorial organisation, and Citluk is within the frame -- comes within the frameworks of that administration. That's how it's set up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I understand that the Judges are always interested, and that gives me pleasure, but all the questions that I have on my list for this witness move in that direction to explain what the administrations are, what the office is, what its relationship to the Defence Department is, what the documents are which bear this out, how appointments are made, what the procedure for that is, and what it was like in practice. So if you will let me move ahead, I think we'll get to those interesting points very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Nozica, I apologise. I plead guilty.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you for your questions, Your Honour, because from the questions you ask, I can see what is important, and then I'll be able to gear my questions towards that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, you performed those duties until July, the chief of the office in Citluk until July 1994, and in that same month, you were appointed chief of the sector for personnel in the personnel administration of the Ministry of Defence of the HR H-B; right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Fine. Now, you stayed in that post until the 1st of January, 1998, when you retired?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. Now let's go back to 1992 again to explain matters. During 1992 when you were the chief of the defence office in Citluk and before you were appointed to the position by the head of the Defence Department, who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: The Croatian Defence Council of Citluk.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Now, after you were appointed chief of the defence office in Citluk in -- at the beginning of 1992, who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: I've already said, the Croatian Defence Council of Citluk was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Either I'm wrong, or it's been recorded wrongly in the transcript. After you were appointed chief of the Citluk Defence Department at the beginning of 1993, after that period, who was your immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1993, my immediate superior was the chief of the defence administration Mostar, and the Citluk defence office came under its jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. Could you give us the name of the person who occupied that post, chief of defence administration of Mostar, because through the documents, that person will no doubt be mentioned.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: At that time, it was Mr. Rade Bosnjak who occupied that post.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Bosnjak, yes. Well, we'll put right the names, but Rade Bosnjak, and was that throughout 1993 that he was chief of the Mostar defence administration?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, during 1992, that is to say from the time you started working in that area, and that was the 1st of June, 1993, to be exact, until July 1994, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, how many administrations for defence were there?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: There was the administration for the defence of Mostar, for the defence of Tomislavgrad, Travnik, and Bosanski Brod, and later on, the administration for the defence of Zepce as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, please, how many defence offices were there within the defence administration of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: There was the Mostar defence. That was Siroki Brijeg, Grude, Ljubuski, Citluk, Ravno, Stolac, Capljina, Neum, and I think in February 1993, Jablanica and Konjic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, in general terms, general terms to start off with, what were the main tasks of the offices and administration of defence during the time that you worked there? Can you list them, the main tasks, and then we'll look at them in greater detail on the basis of the documents I'm going to show you.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, mostly, they were tasks to see that the records for recruits were kept in order, mobilisation, replenishment of units, recording, recruitment, and links with units of the local administration in order to facilitate our work; mobilisation preparation, that is to say the terrain and so on and so forth; and other tasks for the requirements of defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you said record-keeping for recruits, and then you said mobilisation for recruits, replenishment of the units?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes to all that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Recruitment again?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And information and surveillance?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Or monitoring and surveillance?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So this method of work or the tasks that you did, were they regulated by the rules governing the armed forces of HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, this was precisely determined.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you take a look at my first document, which is P 00289, the first document in my binder.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: I don't have any binders.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You will be given them in just a moment. Here they are. May we take a look at the first binder because there are two, binder number 1 and binder number 2, and in one you'll find the first document, the decree governing the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pinjuh, this is a decree dated the 3rd of July, 1993, so can we go through -- 3rd of July, 1992. Can we go through the articles as they affected your area of work, and let's look at Article 7 to begin with. It regulates matters of your material requirements and responsibilities. So did you have tasks within this field as stipulated here?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please look at Article 9, which refers to the powers of the HVO HZ-HB in the area of defence and says under 5: "Enacts regulations on the application and method of carrying out mobilisation of men and materiel." And 6: "Decides on carrying out mobilisation." In your experience, is this how mobilisation was carried out?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please look at Article 10, which refers to the obligations of the Defence Department and which says that the Defence Department carries out tasks relating to points 9 and 18, items 9 and 18. Mr. Pinjuh, we have seen these documents more than once, so I will not dwell on them long, but under 9 it says the mobilisation and manpower levels of the armed forces and then also material obligations. Is that what it says here?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In item 18 it says: Ensuring the reinforcement and mobilisation of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, or, rather, the bringing up to manpower levels.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, please now look at Article 12, and this is linked to one of the questions asked by Their Honours. It says in Article 12: "To carry out defence tasks ..." and in item 1, it says: "As part of the Defence Department, administrations for defence and offices for defence shall be established."

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So it says the decision on the numbers and headquarters and the areas in which defence administrations and defence offices shall be active will be passed by the HVO at the proposal of the head of defence. Is that how it was, Mr. Pinjuh?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Look at Article 13, which refers to defence administrations and says that these are administrative and military territorial bodies carrying out professional work relating to the armed forces under the guidance of the head of defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And are these tasks enumerated here under numbers 1 to 11?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Under numbers 1 and 2, is this mainly referring to tasks which both administrations and offices dealt with most often in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, almost all the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Article 14 of this decree refers to defence offices which shall be constituent parts of the defence administration and shall in particular perform the following tasks: Keep records of military conscripts, keep the records of materiel and equipment, and introduce conscription for defence needs. I'm cutting this short because everyone can see the text. Are these the main tasks that the offices for defence dealt with? I'm asking you this for you to confirm because you are the chief of one such office.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please now look at Article 33. This refers to raising up to manpower level the armed forces. We have already established that this was one of the main tasks that both the defence offices and defence administrations dealt with; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In Article 33, the procedure for raising the manpower levels is described, and in Article 35, we see that units and institutions are -- have their manpower levels raised according to the military assignments and the priorities, and this is done by the offices for defence?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now we'll move on to other kinds of tasks, which you said also took up quite a lot of your time in 1992 and 1993, and that is mobilisation. Mr. Pinjuh, tell me, how long was mobilisation of the armed forces carried out in 1992 and 1993 while you were working on this?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, in my experience, starting from the 10th of July, 1992, when it was declared, it went on until the end of the war, so mobilisation was carried on on a permanent basis, and it was never fully completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Article 36 says that mobilisation can be general or partial in scope?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Article 37 says that mobilisation shall be ordered by the president of the HZ-HB. That's how it was, Mr. Pinjuh?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Article 38 says the following: "The preparation and implementation of the mobilisation of the armed forces shall be the responsibility of: 1, the head of the Defence Department of the HVO for preparing and implementing the mobilisation of the armed forces and the commanders of staffs, units, and institutions of the armed forces for preparing and implementing the mobilisation of the staffs, units, and institutions under their control and command." Is that how it was, Mr. Pinjuh?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, could we now look at the next document, simply to see whether this was prescribed in another decree, as well, and that is 00588. This is the decree on the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. The document is P - I don't see it in this transcript - P 00588. Yes, I see it now. So this is the decree on the armed forces of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and it is dated from October, the 17th of October, 1992. Have you found it, sir?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very briefly, let's look at Article 7, which is identical to the previous decree that we have seen; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Article 9, it's also identical?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And Article 10, it's identical; is it not?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Except that it's no longer item 18 but item 17 because in the previous decree, the numbers were a little different?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, and there's another difference, as well, in the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Articles 12, 13, and 14, do they also prescribe the same as the previous decree?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's look at Article 33, which deals with raising the units up to manpower level. That's Article 33, 34, and 35. Do they regulate this area in the same way as before?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can see, the provisions are the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There is one change, which is in Article 34.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. 34.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: To be quite precise, it's in paragraph 2, which says that: "Commanders of brigades and high-ranking officers shall be appointed ..." and so on, and Article 35, which refers to defence offices remains the same. Article 36 remains the same. You'll have to confirm because I'm not allowed to testify.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Please excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In Article 37 --

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: It remains the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is there anything added in paragraph 2, so we don't have to go back, Mr. Pinjuh, where it says that the president of the HZ-HB shall order the mobilisation of the armed forces, whereas now a new paragraph has been added which says mobilisation of the armed forces shall be organised in accordance with the plan of mobilisation dynamics and carried out in accordance with plans for the mobilisation of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In Article 38, there is again something new. Have you noticed it? It's in the last paragraph of Article 38.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: It has to do with the regulations?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. And these shall be issued by the head of the Defence Department. Regulations on preparation and execution of mobilisation of the armed forces shall be issued by the head of the Defence Department. All right. So we have seen how things were according to the decree on the armed forces. Mr. Pinjuh, when did the defence administrations begin to be active on the territory HZ-HB?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: In late 1992 and early 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, do you know what document regulated the method of selection of the chiefs of the defence administration and the other operatives and other employees of the offices and administrations?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, there was a decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Can we now look at Document 2D 00567. This is the decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department, and it's dated the 17th of October, 1992. Please take a look at item 8. We've already said that the administrations and offices were active within the scope of the Defence Department, and here we shall see who was in charge of these administrations and offices and how the people were appointed. It says here that the chief of the administration shall be in charge, and he shall be responsibile to the head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Is that how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it says here chiefs of Defence Departments are appointed by the HVO of the HZ-HB at the proposal of the head of the Defence Department. Is that how it was, Mr. Pinjuh, or was there another chain here in -- another link in the chain in practice?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, the municipality where the Defence Department had its seat participated with its approval.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It further says assistant chiefs in the defence administration shall be appointed by the head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All other operatives and employees in the defence administration shall be assigned by the chief of the administration with the approval of the head of the Defence Department or a person authorised by him.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now, we'll move on to defence offices which are mentioned in item 9. It says here that chiefs of the defence office manages the work of the defence office, and he is responsible for his work directly to the chief of the defence administration.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And through the chief of the defence administration to the head and deputy head of the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And we are now coming to the question of His Honour Judge Antonetti. It says here the chief of the defence administration -- defence office shall be appointed by the chief of the defence administration, or, rather, he shall be appointed by the head of the Defence Department with the approval of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And then it says here all other operatives and employees and the defence officer are appointed by the chief of the defence office of the approval of the Defence Department. You did that?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Or a person authorised by him and with the opinion of the chief of the competent defence administration; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the opinion of the head of the defence administration was sought. So Mr. Pinjuh, the procedures were as described here with the addition made by you in the case of the selection of the chief of defence administrations?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you now please take a look at the next document. We won't dwell on it, but let's look at it. It's P 02477. It's the decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department of the 20th of May, 1993. Mr. Pinjuh, we have -- or, rather, you have looked at this decision, and as regards the manner of selection of officers in -- or, rather, employees in both the offices and administrations for defence, there were no changes here in relation to the previous documents?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at 2D 1199, please. 2D 1199. Yes. It's correct in the transcript. Mr. Pinjuh, you have before you a document signed by the head of the Defence Department, and it's a proposal for the appointment of the head of the defence administration for Mostar, who was your superior; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So this proposal is addressed to the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it says that it is based on -- it's issued pursuant to provision to the provisions of item 7 of the resolution, and it says that it proposes that Mr. Rade Bosnjak from Mostar be appointed the head of the defence administration who had served up until then as the head of the HVO municipal headquarters in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it says: "I also inform you that we have received a positive opinion from the Croatian Defence Council from Mostar municipality regarding this proposal."

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, you know that this is the procedure through which Mr. Bosnjak was appointed?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's look at 2D 1225. You have seen many such decisions. They are all identical, and because of the shortage of time, I have selected only two to illustrate to the Court whether this was the model used for all appointments.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Here we have a document signed again by the head of the Defence Department, and it's dated the -- it's January 1993, and he is issuing a decision in the office for defence in Odzak municipality. Slavko Bago is appointed head of the defence office in Odzak, and in the statement of reasons, it says: "At the suggestion of the head of the defence administration of Bosanski Brod and with the previous consent of the Croatian Defence Council of Odzak municipality, the head of the Defence Department has decided as previously stated in this decision ..." and we even have here a legal remedy described.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that was the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And were you appointed according to that same procedure?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we couldn't find your letter of appointment, but it would have been the same as this; right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, we have an agreement here, an agreement signed by Mr. Stojic, we saw in which cases he gave his agreement. That is document 2D 1206.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. Whereby Mr. Abdulah Kasim Primeca, born in 1963, be appointed a higher clerk in the Defence Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So this is for the appointment of these individuals, and all that was necessary there was an agreement and consent by the head; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, we've looked at the legal frameworks and the way in which appointments were made, the procedure thereof. Can you explain to the Court how the internal setup, what the internal setup was of the defence administration and office?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: There was a decision and rules of procedure within the frameworks of the offices for defence within HZ-HB, and it regulated all these areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we take a look at document P 00988 now, please. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what kind of decision this is, who brought in this decision, and was it one of the documents you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: It was the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the Croatian Defence Council from 1993 that passed this decision. I can't see the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's fine. But as it says in the preamble, it's the HVO HZ-HB who is making this decision; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we look at a decision that you mentioned -- or rather, this is the document you mentioned. Now let's look at P 1553 next, please.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: It is regulations on the internal organisation of the defence offices and administrations on the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and it is passed by the head of the Defence Department, Mr. Bruno Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, Mr. Pinjuh, let's look at Article 3 of these regulations briefly where it says that a united internal -- that there's a united internal organisation for all the defence offices and united systemisation, that is to say, who occupies what post and so on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, look at Article 4, please. And it says that a uniformed sector for the defence offices are prescribed for the municipalities depending on the number and seats, and we have the work post set out for people working in those offices; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And this brings us to the question of regulating the headquarters of the administrations and offices and who passed this decision, what the administrations -- defence administrations are, and what the offices are.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: The HVO HZ-HB makes the decision as to the number of people working in the general area and the number of offices or administrations.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's now look at P 00700. It is a proposal for decision on the number of seats for the -- and headquarters for the defence offices and so on. Is this proposed by the head of the department to the HVO HZ-HB; right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. And as far as I remember, there were two more, two other amendments to the proposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: For the transcript, I'd like to emphasise that all these decisions are ones that we showed to witness Slobodan Bozic, so there's no need for us to go through them all again. But just look at the next document, which is P 00767, and it is the minutes from the 11th session of the Croatian Defence Council dated the 18th of November, 1992, and under point 4 we see that there was a discussion of this proposal and that it was adopted after a debate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pinjuh, you said that there were two other amendments. Can you confirm what these amendments were, if you remember, and can you confirm whether the same procedure was applied for those amendments?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: I remember that in February in the defence administration of Mostar, Konjic and Jablanica were attached, and in the second amendment it was the formation of the 5th administration for the defence of Zepce with all the attendant defence offices, and the procedure was the same once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, Mr. Pinjuh, as the chief of the defence office, did you compile any reports, and if so, what kind of reports were they, and who did you send them to? Who were they addressed to?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, we did compile six monthly and annual reports, and we sent them to the defence administration, which was in my case the Mostar administration, and then they would send them on to the head and deputy of the Defence Department. As far as I know, they were also used in reports written for the government sessions of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you compile any other periodical reports, for example, except for these half-yearly and yearly reports?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, if the administration required and if the circumstances and situation required it as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, let's look at document P 4699, which is a report on the work of the Croatian Defence Council for the period from January to June 1993.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And in that report, take a look at page 5, please, of the Croatian version, and it is page 3 of the English. And it talks about the Mostar administration area, which is the area to which your office belonged, and we can see that from the first sentence there. I'm just going to point out certain sections, and we'll comment later, and I think this is important. Let's see if that was the case. "In its work ..." and that's the second sentence of paragraph 1. "In its work, it paid special attention to the recruitment, reinforcement, and mobilisation of reservists." Now, Mr. Pinjuh, they are the basic tasks that you yourself mentioned at the beginning of your testimony here this afternoon; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "This administration will have final and exact date on the 19th of July, 1993, by which time mobilisation is to be completed in all the municipalities except Mostar. In the next period, its activities will be directed at the municipality of Mostar..." and then it says: "... for well known reasons." Now, Mr. Pinjuh, tell us, please, can you remember what those well known reasons were which had a bearing on the fact that in this Mostar administration report those reasons are mentioned?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, I remember that on the 30th of June, 1993, members of the Croatian Defence Council who were Muslims by ethnicity disarmed their combatants, Croats, from the HVO and that in actual fact this was a declaration of war on the Croatian Defence Council in the area. And that is why the reports -- the order of the reports was disrupted, and that's why there wasn't better information in Mostar at the time. There was a general disruption.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, did these events influence the further work towards mobilisation in the area, especially when it came to the area under the Mostar defence administration?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, yes, certainly, because in 1991 when the aggression by the Serb army started in the territory of the HZ-HB, units were established on the basis of volunteers, and both Croats and other ethnicities manned those units. However, after this particular event, it wasn't realistic to expect the Muslims to respond to the call-up for the HVO units, and that's why it disrupted the situation in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, we'll come back to those issues, but I'll move on and look at the report some more. It says here that the Home Guards question was resolved in the shortest possible time. Now, we'll talk about Home Guards later on, but were you involved in this work?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Fine. It says on the basis of the decision to train recruits, and your name is mentioned, and it says how many recruits responded and what training courses were organised. So were you involved in that work too, Mr. Pinjuh?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Look at page 7, please, of the Croatian version, and that is page 5 in the English. Once again, paragraph 3 on page 5. Page 5 in the English, please. Have you found page 7?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There's an observation made here. For the efficient work of the administrations and defence offices, there must be a proper record of personnel and materiel and technical equipment, and the chiefs come across -- of the departments come across various difficulties in their work in collecting information about recruits who were mobilised in different ways without the knowledge of and recording by the office of people who are registered as recruits.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that's what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What was it? Where was the problem? Where did the problem lie? What was the problem here because this relates to the problems that the defence office was encountering.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: To a great extent, the fact that people went into the units and left units without any record of that being kept, that was a problem. People tried to avoid the call-up. They would give false addresses and things like that, so it was very difficult to keep abreast of the situation and keep a proper and timely record of the recruits.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So that was a continuous problem, was it, of the office in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, throughout 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, we still have time before the break, and I think that we can try and go into another very important area. And I'm going to question you about the Home Guards and Home Guard units and how that was resolved, and I think that through my questions, we'll be able to answer the question of how the manpower levels were brought up to scratch. Now, in the 1993 report, we saw that the manpower levels were replenished in the briefest space of time. Can you explain to the Court how this issue was resolved in actual fact?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, the president of the HZ-HB, Mr. Boban, passed a decision on the establishment of the Home Guards and their units, and on the basis of that decision, the defence office and the Main Staff through their own chains of command acted upon that, and specifically when we were concerned, the defence office would precisely define -- we were given precise assignments in that whole process and procedure, and that's why we were able to get through it fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at the first document from this series, and then we'll continue discussing how this was done technically. It was P 00680. Document P 00680. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a decision on the establishment of the Home Guards passed by Mate Boban, president of the HZ-HB, on the 3rd of November, 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, tell us two things: What were the tasks of these Home Guard units, and who were the members of those Home Guard units? Who became a member of the Home Guards?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: The members of the Home Guard units were supposed to be military recruits who didn't -- which -- who did not have their wartime schedule, wartime assignment, which meant that they were mostly elderly persons, and their task was to guard important features, roads, and so on and everything that was important to ensure the normal -- normal life in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's look at some of these articles under this decision, or, rather, we are going to comment them later on, but let's read some out. Article 5, it says: "Units and headquarters of the Home Guard shall be subordinated to the commands of operational zones" -- "operative zones and to the General Staff" -- to the Main Staff in the chain of command." Then Article 6 says: "Upon this decision coming into force, those eligible for military service who have not been assigned their wartime stations shall be transferred to the units of the Home Guards." Is that it?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And Article 7 says: "The head of the Defence Department shall have the authority to prescribe regulations and draw up mobilisation plans for the Home Guard."

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, let's look at the next document following this decision, and it is P 1424.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to come back to the Domobrani, the Home Guards. We've heard other witness, many witnesses. In fact, we've spent thousands of hours in this case, so now we have more precise knowledge of certain events. We know that several prisons were guarded by individuals who came under this category. They were older, and, therefore, they were asked to do that task. I see that under Article 5, it states that these individuals were commanded by the operational zone and the Main Staff. In your opinion, a Domobrani who is assigned to guarding a prison, what line of command does he come under?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my opinion, their unit which sent them there, the unit they belong to, and above that unit should be the operative zone or higher up.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked to you look at document P 1424. It wasn't recorded in the transcript. It's an order, as you explained, and it says that the head of the Defence Department issued one such order -- a decision, rather, and the second one was issued by the chief of the Main Staff. So is this the decision issued by the -- by the head of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, here we can see an explanation as to why these units are being established, and under 3 it says here that companies, battalions, and regiments were established; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And this document was delivered to the Defence Department in Mostar, Tomislavgrad, Travnik and Bosanski Brod. Is this what you explained, that the department then sent the order down the chain?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, then, let's look at 01441. This is an order issued by the chief of the Main Staff referring to the order issued by the head of the Defence Department of the 5th of February as regards the establishment of Home Guard units. Can you comment on this? What is this about?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, this is going down his chain of command to the operative zones that he was in command of.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, what was the task of the defence office, if you can explain very briefly, as regards this order? What specifically did the offices do pursuant to this order? What did your office do, to be precise?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, in the first place, the office would carry out the call-up according to the order pursuant to the plan, according to the military occupational specialties or arms of service, and when a list had been drawn up of those who had responded to the call-up, the list would be delivered together with the files of these men to the Home Guard unit which was being established.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'll ask you to look at P 1587. That is a document signed by the chief of the defence administration Rade Bosnjak, and it concerns the establishment of Home Guard units, and it refers both to the order issued by the head of the Defence Department because as you explained, this was sent to the administrations which further forwarded it to the offices, and this one was delivered to the Konjic Jablanica office. But what concerns us here is item 2, which explains how the operative units of the HVO armed forces are brought up to manpower level according to the mobilisation plan, and it says that this is to be carried out in accordance with Article 78, 14, 34, 35, and 110 of the aforementioned decree; the decree is the decree on the armed forces; Article 17 and 80 of the rules on carrying out compulsory military service; Article 9 of the decision on the internal organisation of the Defence Department; and it concludes that all requests for reinforcement or -- for reinforcement must be forwarded to this administration via the OZ OR MOB, south-east Herzegovina zone of operations to this administration. Mr. Pinjuh, can we first clarify the following: I'm interested in this last sentence where Mr. Bosnjak says that all requests for reinforcement must be forwarded through the zone of operations, and he mentions the OR MOB. What does OR MOB refer to, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: It's the organisational and mobilisational affairs department, which was part of the zone of operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it says delivered or forwarded to this administration?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. That should be the proper route and the proper procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Can you explain to Their Honours what documents were necessary and had to be passed before a request for reinforcement could be put in, so on what basis could reinforcement of units of the HVO be carried out?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, first, there had to be plan of replenishment or reinforcement, and this plan was based on assessments and proposal by the department for establishment of the Main Staff, which forwarded it to the administration for military conscripts and mobilisation, which then drew up the reinforcements plan. It would send the plan back to the military territorial commands and the administration for defence, and they would send then excerpts from this order to the offices that had these tasks within their purview.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The administration for military conscription and mobilisation, was it part of the civilian part of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, please tell us now who had to submit a request for bringing military units up to manpower levels and to whom?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: To bring up to manpower levels the military units, the requests had to be submitted by the zones of operations to the administration, and the administration would then forward this to the offices carrying out the reinforcement, and we have seen that in the instructions issued by Mr. Rade Bosnjak.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's the one we're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, were there other kind of requests? For example, did brigades write directly to the defence offices? Were there instances where this procedure was deviated from in practice?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were such instances. I have to say that there were, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, we'll deal with that later. When you were talking about the proposal for the plan --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've tried to understand exactly what your role was. As I look at the document on the screen and also the document P 700, if I understand correctly - and please do tell me if I misunderstood something because it's very important - at the very top, you have the department of defence with Mr. Stojic. Then underneath, there are four departments of the defence administration. You have Mostar. You have Tomislavgrad, Travnik, and Bosanski Brod. And in the department of the administration of Mostar, there are nine districts: Stolac, Ravno, Capljina, Neum, Vuski [phoen], Grude, Siroki Brijeg, Citluk, and Mostar. And if I've understood correctly, you were the head in Citluk of the -- of that department of the administration. Have I understood correctly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've understood correctly, you confirm?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Very good. So you see I've followed very closely.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, you said a little while ago that the mobilisation plan was issued by the department for mobilisation of the Main Staff, and then it was sent to the administration for conscripts and mobilisation, and based on that they drew up a plan. So let's now look at the armed forces from the Main Staff to brigade level. Who dealt with tasks concerning mobilisation and reinforcement? Let's look at document P 00502.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's the next binder. Sorry, it's my fault for not mentioning it. Mr. Bruno Stojic now here prescribes a temporary establishment of the Main Staff. Can we look at positions 44, 46, 47, and 48, please. Could you just comment on that? So 44, it says here above 44 the department for organisation, personnel, and legal affairs, and then there's a chief and a secretary; and 47 is an organisational officer; and then there's mobilisation; and 48 is the officer for reinforcements.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Is this what you were referring to when you were mentioning the proposal for the plan of reinforcement?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we please look at document 2D 927, and could you please look at positions 21, 22, 23, and I will only say that this is also a document dated the 10th of December, 1992, and signed by Mr. Stojic, and it's an interim establishment of the command of the zone of operations. As these are all abbreviations, could you please tell us who these persons are in the positions I mentioned and whether they were working on tasks having to do with mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. The assistant commander for organisational mobilisation and personnel affairs, then there's a desk officer, a lawyer, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the next document. That's 2D 01370.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a diagram showing the brigade establishment. You have page 3 under 1 and 2, and in English, it's page 5, 1 and 2. Could you please tell me on page 3, under 1 and 2, whether these -- this is the organisational mobilisational department?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes. Officer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: These were the assistant commander for organisation and mobilisation and personnel affairs and then officer dealing with the same affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I have only two other documents to deal with in this area, and then if it's time for a break, we can take a break. Sir, did you have contacts in your offices for defence with the members of the commands of the units which were in the area of Citluk municipality as regards both mobilisation and bringing up to manpower levels? Did you have to have contacts with them?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, we did have contacts with them, especially with the officers dealing with mobilisation and personnel affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, the officer was the person who receives the list and the files of the men and handles them, and he is a very important person in communication when there is an exchange of information about people leaving and coming and going for different reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, I asked you whether there were any deviations from the regular procedure as regards reinforcing the units or, rather, bringing up to manpower level, and people applying not to the proper body.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at document 1223, please. 2D 1223.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We might say that this is an example of the way things were sometimes done.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, I was waiting for my question and your answer to be recorded in the transcript. This is a request dated the 2nd of April, 1993, for bringing up to manpower levels the battalion in Neum, and it's signed by Nedeljko Obradovic. According to the practice and the instructions issued by Mr. Rade Bosnjak, could the brigade commander request reinforcements of men and do so by applying to the chief of the office directly?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: No. He should have done this through the zone of operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And to whom should he have applied, to the office or to the administration for defence?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: To the administration for defence, which would then have forwarded whatever referred to the offices to the offices because there are all sorts of things mentioned here, the civilian police and things to do with medical examinations and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now we are dealing only with bringing up to manpower levels. Let's please look at document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am afraid it's time for the break. 20 minutes' break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Court is in session. There has be a slight correction to the transcript on page 2, line 4. There should be 25 rather than 27. 25th of February, 2009, to be perfectly accurate. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, I've been told that we tend to speak quickly, either I in asking my questions or you in the answers, so the court reporter has a problem there. So I want to ask you to slow down or, rather, to make pauses between questions and answers. Mr. Pinjuh, before the break, we were discussing the request coming in from the first brigade of the HVO with respect to reinforcement and manpower levels for the brigade, and let's just remind ourselves, you were saying that that was not in conformity with procedure or practice, so take a look at P 01880 next, please, which is a letter, which the head of the Mostar defence administration, Mr. Rade Bosnjak, is sending to Mr. Bruno Stojic the head of the Defence Department, on the 15th of April, 1993, in which he refers to the request we saw a moment ago under number 2D 1223. Now, Mr. Pinjuh, does Mr. Bosnjak indicate here that requests of that kind are not in conformity with procedure? I think that we'll find that on page 2, so can you give us your opinions about that?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, I think that the head of the defence administration here has stipulated that there has been a violation of regulations in violation of procedural regulations, and according to what it says here, latterly, he is very strict in expressing this, and I would even say that he bringing into question the need for administrations and offices to exist at all if that's the way they are going to be working.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. We are going to move on to another area now, and it is this: In the report for the first half of 1993, the biannual report, or, rather, six-monthly report in which the administration for defence of Mostar says that it has conducted certain affairs with respect to recruitment. Can you tell me what these tasks were and whether you in the defence office were involved in any way in this work?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, we were involved. Certainly we were, and the work involved introducing the new people into the records, the dates of birth. I think that it was 1975, people born in 1975 and some older people who failed to become soldiers so that all this was done on the basis of the regulations governing civilian service and military service. So we accomplished this task fairly quickly and I would say fairly well too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, you mentioned that this was done according to the military services and civilian services duties. Can you look at 2D 1232 next, please. Are those the rules that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you look at Article 17 to 33 and tell us whether they are provisions which relate to recruits and the procedure that you spoke about?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, those are the articles.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at document 2D 1023 next, please, which is a decision dated the 7th of June, 1993, signed by Mr. Bruno Stojic and in which he says that teaching centres for training should be formed for the south-east Herzegovina operation zone; the centres for training in the Capljina base and the Heliodrom base; and then for north-west Herzegovina, that operation zone; training centres are to be formed in Crvenice, Tomislavgrad municipality; and under number 2, coordination of the preparation of the centre for uninterrupted taking-in of recruits for appropriate working conditions and residence will be conducted by the Main Staff headquarters using the operational zones and heads of training centres. Now, can you explain to us why such a decision was necessary in the first place when recruits were being called up and taken in and trained and the courses, training courses that were to be put in place?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, it was necessary to ensure the right premises for accommodation and also for training for the new recruits, first of all, basic training and then more specialised training courses, so that when they had completed all that, they could be said to have completed the military service.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now look at 2D 1210, please. That's the next document. It is a letter once again from the head of the Mostar administration, Rade Bosnjak, sent on the 15th of July, 1993, to the head, Mr. Bruno Stojic, and it is -- it concerns certain recruitment affairs. So could you tell us whether something had to be done before the recruits were sent off for training?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Certainly. And from this, we can see that not everything functioned properly at all levels. However, all the recruits had to sit for a medical examination, and a recruitment -- sit before a recruitment commission, and I can see from this letter from Mr. Bosnjak that he speaks about problems in certain health institutions with respect to recruits and recruitment, probably medicines, something to do with medicines and the resources necessary and everything concerning a proper medical examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's look at the last document in this area, which is P 4091 [Realtime transcript read in error, "B"]. It's not B; it's P for the transcript. 4091. Yes, that's right. Unfortunately, my time is limited, so I won't be able to look at this in any great detail, but this is an order for specialised training.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And from this, does it follow that basic training was conducted for recruits before this, and then that there were specialist training courses for recruits as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, can you tell me, Mr. Pinjuh, who was in charge of recruitment training? Did that come under the offices or the administration, or who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: For training, it was the department for education and training attached to the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pinjuh, let's take a look at document P 7433, and I'm going to ask you to explain to the Court what this is. What kind of document is this?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: This is an annual analysis of the performance of the Mostar defence administration for 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, let's take a look at page 3. It's also page 3 in English. And tell us, please, what in this annual analysis report does it say on page 3, under defence administration tasks, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, it sets out the legal grounds for establishing the administrations and offices for defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Will you look at page 13 in the Croatian version now, which is page 9 in the English, and explain to the Court what we see on that page.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: This page shows the structure of the people working there for the Citluk defence office, and I was the head of the office, so the employees there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. May we look at the next page, and on the next page, Mr. Pinjuh, is a review of the combat engagement for recruits in Citluk municipality, and it says also in percentages in relation to the number of military recruits in the military records. Now, questions like this have already been raised in this courtroom, and I'm going to ask you the question directly because I assume you compiled this.

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The first line says that the number of Croat inhabitants according to the 1991 population census was the number it says here. Now, why was an analysis conducted according to the number of Croat inhabitants, this analysis, this particular analysis that you said was done at the end of 1993? Why does it only mention Croat inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, I've already said that so let me repeat, that on the 30th of June, 1993, the incident that I mentioned before took place whereby the members of the HVO who were Muslims captured their fellow fighters from the HVO, their fellow combatants, and after that all the analyses which would be different would not provide a realistic picture of the people who were in the military.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, regardless of the national ethnic structure of Citluk municipality, we'll come to that later on, but in the area in general, the area covered by the Mostar defence administration, after the 30th of June, could they count on members of the -- of Muslim ethnicity as being members of HVO units?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: As far as I know, yes, some of them remained in HVO units until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you, Mr. Pinjuh. I'm asking you something else. Yes, some did stay on, but what I'm asking you is this: In the area covered by the Mostar administration after the 30th of June, could the HVO count on the Muslim members -- could Muslims be engaged in HVO units?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Ah, no, not that, no. They could not.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, tell me, in the Citluk municipality area, what was the ethnic structure in 1991 there?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Well, I'll not quite sure whether there were more than 1 to 2 percent of Serbs and others, perhaps a little larger percentage of Muslims. It was almost an ethnically pure Croat environment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pinjuh, do you know whether on the territory covered by the Mostar defence administration whether there were Muslims within the HVO units before the 30th of June, 1993, and after that?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: Yes, I know that some of them remain there until the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us now take a look at page 43 of this same report, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a technical detail. In Citluk, while we have the list of all the people who were with you, now, number 5, Kruno [phoen] Stojic, is he a relative of Mr. Stojic's or not? His first name is Kruno.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, they have nothing to do with each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And number 12, Ivan Pinjuh, is this person a relative of yours or not? He was in charge of correspondence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, he wasn't a relative or relation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] thank you. And thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the gentleman mentioned under number 12 was Teklic [phoen], so he was a courier, was he? Would you explain that to us briefly? What did Mr. --

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: He took 'round the invitations, mostly, call-ups.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I asked you to take a look at page 43, which is page 32 of the English, and can you explain to the Trial Chamber what we have on that page in this general analysis?

utterances.speaker: BRUNO PINJUH
utterances.text: This page shows the internal structure of the defence administration and defence office.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Take a look at the next page now, please. This is a diagram of the internal structure of the defence administration for Mostar. That's a chart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You would be very kind if you indicated the pages in the English version because I think it's not what you've told us.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said that it was page 32 and the following pages, that is to say 33, 34.
